films.title: Sugar High
films.description: Welcome Skateboards' 23-minute team full-length centers the loose, social side of skating: friends, missed tricks, late nights and rolling without a scoreboard. The complete first-party billing preserves all 11 featured skaters, while Jeremy Creed receives the principal filming and editing credits.
creditNotes: Welcome's official upload supplies the complete 11-name featured billing and explicitly credits Jeremy Creed with principal filming and editing.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies Sugar High as a 24-minute full-length, confirms the soundtrack section structure, identifies Bevup as Nathan Ko and credits Jeremy Creed and Daniel Vargas as filmmakers.
TransWorld independently identifies all 11 appearances, distinguishes Nick Garcia and Ryan Reyes as Welcome's newest recruits and credits the video to Jeremy Creed.
Jake Yanko appears in Welcome's first-party featured billing and is retained even though SkateVideoSite's indexed skater count omits him.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite catalogs the film as a United States production; no narrower location list is asserted from the footage alone.
films.historicalContext: Welcome framed Sugar High as a deliberate celebration of friendship and fun over competitive escalation. Contemporary TransWorld coverage treated it as a new company full-length and highlighted its entire current squad.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is a dedicated neon Sugar High title card from the authorized film, with no trailer, episode or event labeling.

films.title: Today Tomorrow Forever
films.description: Foundation Skateboards' 22-minute team film was directed and edited by Don Luong after roughly two years of work. Six principal parts carry the film, while an F Block montage adds four further credited appearances; the official end titles also preserve 17 additional camera contributors.
creditNotes: Foundation's official upload supplies the six principal riders and the release date.
A visual review of the official end titles explicitly confirms 'Directed and Edited by Don Luong,' identifies the four additional F Block appearances and preserves all 17 names on the camera card.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies the release as a 22-minute full-length, credits Don Luong as principal filmmaker and confirms the six principal sections and their order.
The PLATFRM's behind-the-scenes feature independently documents the two-year production and identifies Don Luong behind the lens.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite catalogs the film as a United States production. The official thumbnail visibly identifies one Encinitas location, but no unsupported comprehensive city list is inferred.
films.historicalContext: The two-year project was Foundation's sixth video in ten years. Its title revives the dedication from Foundation's 2001 Art Bars: Subtitles and Seagulls, while the premiere marked Ruby Lilley's promotion to professional status.
premiereNotes: The film premiered in May 2026 before its official online release on May 22.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload exposes a 480x360 YouTube thumbnail rather than a valid max-resolution image. It was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16 and shows a skater above the Encinitas City Hall sign from the film, with no misleading trailer, episode or event text.

Contemporary Don Luong interview documents the film's creative direction, Jessie Darnall's first major video, Ruby Lilley's pro surprise, the title's Art Bars origin and Foundation's six-video decade.

films.title: A Guided Tour
films.description: ASICS Skateboarding's 25-minute global full-length was directed and edited by Jacob Harris, with Jake Gascoyne shaping its creative framework. Five skaters receive principal parts and 20 more appear across montage and supporting sections filmed over eight months from Helsinki and Okinawa to Los Angeles and New York City.
creditNotes: Contemporary release coverage identifies five principal parts and 20 additional montage/supporting appearances; all 25 are retained and distinguished here.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies the release as a 26-minute ASICS full-length, credits Jacob Elliott Harris as principal filmmaker and corroborates the section structure.
Jacob Harris' first-person VHSMAG interview directly discusses filming and editing A Guided Tour and explains its wellness framing.
Premiere coverage explicitly credits Jacob Harris as director and Jake Gascoyne with shaping the creative framework.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: Contemporary premiere coverage explicitly identifies the four filming destinations and states that production spanned eight months.
films.historicalContext: A Guided Tour was ASICS Skateboarding's third full-length and one of its most ambitious projects, introducing Jaakko Ojanen, Kyonosuke Yamashita, Evan Wasser and Victor Campillo to the roster through a satirical but sincere wellness-themed travel framework.
premiereNotes: A community premiere took place on September 13, 2025 before the worldwide online release on September 17.
films.artworkNotes: The authorized Thrasher upload's 1280x720 max-resolution YouTube thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is an unaltered landscape action frame from the exact full film, with no trailer, episode or event text.
